758	## ADDENDUM 4 (2026-07-26, run 0048 round 4) — the on-stratum witness EXISTS, and R1 is correct exactly when `|P¹(k)| ≥ g + 2` (BINDING; closes I-0356 and answers I-0346)
759	
760	ADDENDUM 3's second corrigendum left one question: the no-go's argument is degree-agnostic, but
761	its only exhibited witness (`F = tX² + XY + tY²` over `k[t]`, `C = P¹`, `π = id`) has degree 2 on a
762	curve of genus 0, off the stratum the functor pins. At `g = 0` the no-go is vacuous, at `g = 1`
763	the base can be shrunk to confine, and at `g ≥ 2` nobody had exhibited anything. This addendum
764	settles it, corrects the argument ADDENDUM 3 used for shrink-stability, and — the part that
765	actually decides the route — gives a sharp iff for R1.
766	
767	### 4.1 First, the criterion ADDENDUM 3 used is the wrong one
768	
769	ADDENDUM 3 argued shrink-stability as "the divisor stays irreducible over every nonempty open of
770	the base, so no Zariski shrink evades the no-go". That is true of the exhibited family and it is
771	not the right criterion, because `IsLocallyCertified` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyZar.lean:71`) asks for
772	a **span-⊤ family**, i.e. a *cover* — and a cover cannot delete a point. The correct criterion is
773	
774	> (★) there is a point `s ∈ Spec R` such that for **every** open `U ∋ s`, some connected component
775	> of `supp(D|_U)` meets both `π⁻¹(p₀)` and `π⁻¹(p₁)`.
776	
777	Under the criterion ADDENDUM 3 actually stated, the campaign's own genus-0 example would be
778	*evaded*: the two witness points of `tX² + XY + tY²` are `([1:0], 0)` and `([0:1], 0)`, both lying
779	over `t = 0`, and over `t ≠ 0` the roots are `(−1 ± √(1−4t²))/2t`, which are never `0` or `∞`. So
780	`D` restricted to `𝔸¹ ∖ {0}` misses *both* pinned fibres. It is a genuine counterexample only
781	because a cover must contain `t = 0`. The conclusion was right; half the reason was missing.
782	
783	### 4.2 The reduction (general — no hypotheses on `k`, `C`, `π`, `n`)
784	
785	Let `S = supp D ⊆ C ×_k Spec R`. Since `D` is finite flat of degree `n` over `R`, `S → Spec R` is
786	finite, hence closed. For `c ∈ P¹(k)` set `W_c :=` the image in `Spec R` of `S ∩ (π⁻¹(c) × Spec R)`
787	— a closed subset. Then for `s ∈ Spec R`:
788	
789	* `s ∉ W_c` ⟹ `U := Spec R ∖ W_c` is an open neighbourhood of `s` on which `supp(D|_U)` misses
790	  `π⁻¹(c)` entirely, i.e. `D|_U` is confined to the chart complementary to `π⁻¹(c)`;
791	* `s ∈ W_c` ⟹ *every* `U ∋ s` has `supp(D|_U)` meeting `π⁻¹(c)`.
792	
793	And `s ∈ W_c ⟺ supp(D_s)` meets `π⁻¹(c)`, a purely **fibrewise** condition. Since `D_s` is finite
794	of degree `n` over `κ(s)`, the image of `supp(D_s)` in `|P¹_k|` has **at most `n` closed points**.
795	
796	Two consequences worth stating separately.
797	
798	**(A) Necessity of `g ≥ 2`.** A witness needs one `s` whose fibre meets both `π⁻¹(p₀)` and
799	`π⁻¹(p₁)`, hence `n ≥ 2`. At `n = g = 1`, `W_{p₀} ∩ W_{p₁} = ∅`, so
800	`{Spec R ∖ W_{p₀}, Spec R ∖ W_{p₁}}` is a *confining cover*. That is I-0356's `g = 1` verdict, now
801	with a proof rather than an observation.
802	
803	**(B) Connectedness is the second half.** The two witness points must lie in the same connected
804	component of `supp(D|_U)` for every `U ∋ s` — equivalently in the same connected component of
805	`S ×_R O_{R,s}`, idempotents of a finite algebra descending to a finite level. Reducible
806	constructions therefore fail: if `S = Δ ∪ ({b} × T)`, a certifier just shrinks until the
807	components separate.
808	
809	### 4.3 The witness, over an arbitrary field
810	
811	Hypotheses: `k` **any** field; `C/k` smooth proper geometrically irreducible of genus `g ≥ 2`;
812	`π : C → P¹` any finite dominant map; `p₀ ≠ p₁ ∈ P¹(k)` the pinned pair.
813	
814	1. `Div^g_{C/k} ≅ Sym^g C =: T` exists over `k` — smooth projective, geometrically irreducible of
815	   dimension `g` — carrying a universal relative effective Cartier divisor `D_univ ⊆ C ×_k T`,
816	   finite flat of degree `g` over `T` (Kleiman, *The Picard scheme*, FGA Explained §9.3; BLR
817	   §8.2/9.3). Every degree-`g` relative divisor over every `R` is a pullback of `D_univ`, so this
818	   analysis is exhaustive rather than a lucky example.
819	2. **`supp D_univ` is irreducible over any `k`**: it is the image of the finite surjection
820	   `C × Sym^{g−1}C → C × Sym^g C`, `(x, ξ) ↦ (x, x + ξ)`, and `C × Sym^{g−1}C` is irreducible
821	   because `C` is geometrically irreducible. No monodromy argument and no `k = k̄` is used.
822	3. **The straddling point.** `π` finite dominant gives closed points `q₀ ∈ π⁻¹(p₀)`,
823	   `q₁ ∈ π⁻¹(p₁)`. Let `L` be a residue field of `κ(q₀) ⊗_k κ(q₁)`, so `L/k` is finite and admits
824	   `k`-embeddings of both; get `Q₀, Q₁ ∈ C(L)` over `p₀, p₁`. Since `g ≥ 2`,
825	   `ξ := (g−1)Q₀ + Q₁` is effective of degree exactly `g`, i.e. an `L`-point of `T`; let `s` be
826	   the underlying closed point. **No rational-point hypothesis is used anywhere** — the padding is
827	   by multiples of `Q₀`, so no "an effective divisor of degree `m` exists over `k`" problem arises,
828	   and `s` is in general not `k`-rational.
829	4. `T` is quasi-projective; choose an affine open `Spec R ⊆ T` containing `s` and put
830	   `D := D_univ|_{Spec R}`. This is on-stratum: degree `g = n`, finite flat over `R`.
831	5. **Non-confinability.** Let `{D(g_i)}` be any span-⊤ family. Some `D(g_i)` contains `s`. Then
832	   `supp(D|_{D(g_i)})` is a nonempty open of the irreducible `supp D_univ`, hence irreducible,
833	   hence preconnected, and it contains points over `p₀` and over `p₁` (the images of `Q₀, Q₁`,
834	   which lie over `s`). By `not_isCertified_of_isPreconnected_of_witnesses`
835	   (`Picard/DivSchemeCertZarVerdict.lean:62`), together with `supportLocus_pullback`
836	   (`DivSchemeCertZarTransport.lean`) and `DivEq.supportLocus_eq` (`DivSchemeCertZarConfine.lean:110`),
837	   no certified family exists over `Localization.Away (g i)` divisor-equal to the pullback. So
838	   `D ∉ DivFamZar(R)` while `D ∈ Div^g_{C/k}(R)`. ∎
839	
840	**Field dependence: none.** It works over `F₂`, over imperfect fields, over non-closed fields.
841	Enlarging `k` does not escape it and neither does descent from a large field — the witness is
842	already there over the small field.
843	
844	### 4.4 The sharp iff for R1, which is the decision this addendum is for
845	
846	The reduction in §4.2 gives, with the pinned pair allowed to vary per cover member (which is
847	exactly what R1 buys):
848	
849	> **R1 is correct if and only if `|P¹(k)| ≥ n + 2`.**
850	>
851	> *If.* For any `D`, `R`, `s`, the image of `supp(D_s)` in `P¹` has at most `n` closed points;
852	> choose `c ∈ P¹(k)` outside it and any `c' ≠ c`. Then `U := Spec R ∖ W_c` confines `D|_U` to the
853	> chart complementary to `π⁻¹(c)`. Doing this at every `s` gives a Zariski cover on which the
854	> divisor is confined, with the pair varying per member.
855	>
856	> *Only if.* If `Σ_{c ∈ P¹(k)} e_c ≤ n`, where `e_c` is the minimal degree of a closed point of `C`
857	> over `c` (e.g. `q + 1 ≤ g` when `C` has a rational point over each `c`), take
858	> `ξ_s = Σ_c q_c + padding`. Then `s ∈ W_c` for **every** `c ∈ P¹(k)`, and no pinned pair confines.
859	
860	This **answers I-0346 exactly, in both directions**; the bound there was a sufficient guess and is
861	now known to be sharp. Consequences for the route:
862	
863	* `p1-aut` / R1 is **not dead**: it is correct over every infinite `k`, and over `F_q` whenever
864	  `q ≥ g + 1`. It is dead exactly over small finite fields.
865	* Because `Challenge.lean:96-99` states the Jacobian over an **arbitrary** field and
866	  `archon-protected.yaml` forbids adding a hypothesis, R1 alone cannot discharge the challenge. It
867	  must be paired with descent (`dat-g`) or replaced.
868	* **R2 is the only field-uniform fix, and it has a short justification**: `supp D` is finite over
869	  `R`, hence contained in a single affine open of `C ×_k Spec R` (avoidance for families, Stacks
870	  0B8B), so a cover with one straddling piece always exists. Generalising `FinCoverData`'s piece
871	  type to arbitrary affine opens of the relative curve is therefore not a gamble; it is the
872	  statement the geometry already supports.
873	
874	### 4.5 What to do in Lean, and what not to
875	
876	**Do not formalise the witness.** It needs `Sym^g C` / `Hilb^g` with its universal flat divisor.
877	Mathlib has no Hilbert schemes, no symmetric products of schemes and no Picard scheme, and this
878	tree constructs no curve other than `P¹` (`C` is always a variable carrying hypotheses). A concrete
879	genus-2 hyperelliptic witness is not cheaper — it still requires building a non-rational proper
880	curve as a scheme, which has never been done here. The payoff would be a negative statement that
881	changes no theorem.
882	
883	**Do this instead (≈40 lines, and it is the honest statement of the no-go):** strengthen
884	`supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isCertified` (`Picard/DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean:131`) and
885	`not_isCertified_of_isPreconnected_of_witnesses` (`DivSchemeCertZarVerdict.lean:62`) from
886	`IsPreconnected d.supportLocus` to the per-connected-component form. The clopen-trace proof at
887	`DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean:98` already gives it, and the general analysis in §4.2 is stated in
888	those terms.
889	
890	Also: `DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean:170-175`'s docstring model is genus 0 — annotate it as
891	off-stratum and point here.

    refine ConcreteCategory.hom_ext _ _ fun v => ?_
    refine sigmaExtension_ext F (Category.assoc g.unop v J.hom) ?_
    rw [← Functor.map_comp_apply, ← op_comp, ← α.homEquiv_comp]
    exact congrArg α.homEquiv (Over.OverMorphism.ext (by simp))
